# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Board now: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT is red again (it was yellow, now back to red). Wires still 1 yellow 2 blue 3 red. Mute, if you can hear this, please describe in words what the manual says to do, since I cannot interpret gestures alone.

Still no direct word from Mute. Mute speaks and I (Blind) can hear speech, so if Mute gives instructions, it should reach me. Maybe Mute hasn't spoken yet, or Mute's message was sent only "to=deaf" and didn't include me, or Mute is waiting on something.

Since turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf each round, Mute speaks first in every round. If Mute had spoken this round, I should have seen it before Deaf's message in my context, but I only see Deaf's message. That likely means Mute called wait() or sent nothing this round, or sent something not addressed to me and my log only shows what's relevant... Actually the context shows "new arrivals" - if Mute had spoken to me, it would show here. It didn't, so Mute is silent so far.

I'll gesture to Deaf using a simple acknowledgment-safe symbol, but more importantly, I should try prompting Mute for the manual info since Mute can hear my speech (Mute reads manual, cannot speak, but can Mute hear? Mute's restrictions: "cannot speak or touch" - hearing not restricted, so Mute can hear). I'll speak to Mute asking for the rule based on colors, and relay Deaf's info since Mute can't see the bomb.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT currently red (was yellow, toggling), wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red. What does the manual say to do for this light/display/wire combination? Please tell me which wire to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Board now: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT yellow, wires 1 yellow 2 blue 3 red - same as two turns ago. Mute, since you can't be heard by Blind directly, please gesture a single tally count matching a wire number, like one symbol for wire 1, two symbols for wire 2, three for wire 3, so I can relay which wire to cut.

Interesting - Deaf just said "Mute, since you can't be heard by Blind directly" - this implies Mute's speech does NOT reach me. Let me reconsider the channel rules.

Actually rereading: "When you speak, Mute receives it" (that's about MY speaking - my speech only reaches Mute). The rule doesn't explicitly say who receives Mute's speech or Deaf's speech. But general rule: "Speech is a voice... Whoever can hear receives your words." Blind cannot hear per the role table? Wait let me check the table again:

"Deaf: Cannot hear anything, or touch the bomb"
"Mute: Cannot Speak, or touch the bomb"
"Blind: Cannot See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed"

So Blind's restrictions don't mention hearing - Blind CAN hear. But Deaf just stated Blind can't hear Mute directly. That's Deaf's belief, possibly wrong, or perhaps correct because Mute's speech is directed only to specific people, or there's a channel restriction I'm missing.

Actually rereading my own channel description again: "When you speak, Mute receives it." This is oddly stated as if only Mute receives when *I* speak, suggesting maybe speech doesn't broadcast to everyone who can hear - it's channel-restricted specifically per role. Perhaps the actual rule is asymmetric: my speech goes only to Mute, Deaf's gesture goes to Deaf+Mute, etc. Maybe Mute's speech (if Mute could speak) - but Mute CANNOT speak at all! Mute can only read manual, never speak.

That's it - Mute cannot speak, period. So Mute can never give me instructions via speech. Mute must use gestures to communicate, but I can't see gestures either. So Mute can only reach Deaf via gesture, and Deaf must relay to me via speech (since Deaf can speak, and I can hear).

So the relay chain is: Mute (gestures) → Deaf (sees gesture) → Deaf speaks → me (hears).

Deaf is asking Mute to gesture a tally count for the wire number. That's smart. Let me wait for that relay.

```
wait()
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Board now: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT is dark now (new state, was yellow then red then yellow). Wires unchanged: 1 yellow 2 blue 3 red. Mute has sent the same gesture two turns running regardless of light color - two identical tap symbols. My best guess is this means wire 2. Blind, if you have other confirmation from the manual via Mute, prioritize that, but if you need to act, wire 2 blue is my tentative read.

Deaf reports Mute has consistently gestured "two taps" regardless of light changes - suggesting the rule is not light-dependent, just "cut wire 2." Two consecutive identical signals is decent confirmation of intent from Mute.

I have no conflicting info. Blue wire is wire 2. I'll act on this, since Mute's signal has been consistent twice and Deaf's relay makes sense.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
